column1: # optlevel-bench --cycles: the rows whose two counters disagree, adjudicated.
# Instructions retired rank the other 36 rows because they reproduce to 0.001%
# here. These eleven are the ones where that counter is the wrong question. Each
# line is one kernel the flag actually changes, built with the flag on and off,
# measured serially at 9 reads and reported as the minimum.
# cyc% and insn% are both "positive = better with the flag on". Where they
# disagree in sign, cpu time was taken as the tiebreak and the verdict is
#   divmagic / divmod        insn -124.4%, cyc +30.0%, cpu +13.3% (IPC 4.00 vs
#                            1.53). One idiv becomes a multiply-shift sequence:
#                            2.24x the instructions, 13% less time. Stays at 2.
#   builtin-math / mathfun   insn +10.8%, cyc -88.8%, cpu -79.4%. fabs is
#                            lowered through a store-forwarding stall. The row
#                            stays at 1 because -ffast-math must reach the fold
#                            at -O2; the LOWERING is the defect, not the level.
# A cycle delta on a memory-bound kernel whose instruction count did not move
# (loopnest, matmul) is code layout, not the flag: loopnest reads -8.6% for
# reg-color, -8.7% for trunc32 and -8.8% for divmagic with all three at
# insn 0.000%, which is one alignment artifact wearing three names. Those rows
flag                     kernel       cycles_on cycles_off     cyc%    insn%
